pam_001: You can recognise it by its height, tall enough to see over the garden wall from the avenue. It stands in the enclosed garden of the Palacio de Navarra.
pam_002: You can recognise it by its broad, rounded, pollarded crown and a base flaring into a mass of roots big enough for animals to den in. It stands at Orkin, in the Ultzama valley.
pam_003: You can recognise it by the gap where lightning took one of its main limbs, over 26 metres tall. It stands at Eltzaburu, reached by a marked route from Sastrain.
pam_004: You can recognise it as one of two separately declared oaks about 570 metres apart, come upon inside the wood rather than seen from a distance. It stands at Jauntsarats.
pam_005: You can recognise it by its smaller leaves with felted undersides, a dry-country oak distinct from the pedunculate oaks further north. It stands at Azanza, in the Goni valley.
pam_006: You can recognise it in winter by its dead brown leaves still on the branches, dropping only when new growth pushes them off. It stands at Garinoain, in the Valdorba.
